text:
maya: Hey folks — hitting a production issue where our streaming responses occasionally end mid-JSON. Client sees valid SSE up until a partial JSON chunk, then the connection closes. No finish_reason or [DONE] event.

maya: Example from our client logs (we're using the hosted API):
```
event: message
data: {\"id\":\"abc123\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"...continued text\"}}]
\n// next event
event: message
data: {\"id\":\"abc123\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"final sentence\"}}]
\n// connection just closes, no finish_reason, no [DONE]
```

maya: Happens ~1-2% of streams, usually on longer responses (>800 tokens). We also see some clients reconnect and request resume which sometimes gives duplicate tokens.

elle: Sorry you're hitting that, @maya. Can you share a request id / x-request-id from the call or a server trace id? Also which SDK / client lib and region? :slightly_frowning_face:

maya: request id: r-0f7e9c44. Using our node client (axios SSE wrapper), region eu-west-1. I attached a tcpdump and our client stderr (I'll paste trimmed):
```
> curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \\
    \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-lite\"\n...\ndata: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"...\"}}]}\ndata: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"...\"}}]}\n// truncated here, connection RESET by peer (RST)
```

ben: Thanks @maya — that request id is in our logs. I see a 200 response then a TCP RST from the client side at 2026-11-02T15:22:34. There was also a small config deployment 1min earlier to the edge proxy (ingress) that bumped keepalive. @deploy-bot can you confirm recent deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy: edge-proxy-config v2.14 rolled to eu-west-1 at 2026-11-02T15:21:10 by infra-ops. Changes: nginx keepalive=25s -> 15s.

ingrid: That keepalive tweak could cause earlier socket closes during long-lived SSE. If the client or intermediate NAT recycles faster than the server keepalive, we see half-closed sockets and abrupt RSTs, which can manifest as truncated streams.

ingrid: Two quick asks: 1) can you share the raw sequence of bytes around the close (you mentioned tcpdump) and 2) can you reproduce deterministically with the curl command?

maya: I can reproduce ~1/5 runs with this curl: `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-large&max_tokens=1200\"` — about 20% of runs cut off mid-JSON. Attaching tcpdump snippet: `...RST from 10.2.1.45`.

ben: Seems like a correlation: edge-proxy keepalive reduced to 15s; our typical long streams exceed that. When the proxy closes, the runtime flushes partial buffers and the client sees truncated JSON with no finish_reason. We should: 1) roll back keepalive to previous value (25s) in eu-west-1 as mitigation, 2) add server-side finalization where the runtime emits an explicit done event if it detects a proxied close, and 3) add client-side recommendation to retry with dedup token/resume strategy.

elle: For support: I've asked @maya to hold for the rollback and to share affected customer ids. Also asked them to enable their client to handle resume idempotently (we have an examples snippet).

ben: Repro plan for eng-runtime: steps below (I can run locally):
1) Start a long-stream request (max_tokens=1200) against staging edge-proxy with keepalive=15s.
2) Simulate NAT timeout by sending FIN/RST from client ip after 16s idle.
3) Observe SSE events: confirm last event is partial JSON and no finish_reason.
4) Log runtime behavior: did `on_stream_close` detect proxied close? check `stream_id`, `buffer_state`, `finish_reason`.

ben: Patch idea (quick): in the streaming loop, on EPIPE or early socket close, attempt to emit a minimal final event that marks end-of-stream:
```
// pseudo
try {
  stream.send(event)
} catch(earlyClose) {
  // best-effort finalization
  emit(event: \"message\", data: JSON.stringify({id: id, choices:[], finish_reason: \"interrupted\"}))
}
```
ingrid: I'd rather we avoid changing semantics for hosted API without docs. Suggest: 1) roll back edge keepalive immediately, 2) add server metrics to detect occurrence rate, 3) add a graceful best-effort emit in runtime behind a feature flag so we can measure.

elle: Agreed. I'm initiating rollback now. @ben can you open a feature-flagged PR for best-effort final emit + metric? Add an opt-in config so Dedicated customers can enable behavior if desired.

ben: Will do. I'll include unit test that simulates socket close and asserts the metric increments and the feature-flag toggles the final event emission.

maya: Thanks — after rollback I ran 30 curl runs and saw zero truncations in 30. I can confirm our client RST came from an intermediate NAT that had a 16s idle timeout.

elle: Awesome. Action items:
- infra-ops: rollback edge-proxy keepalive to 25s in eu-west-1 (done by 15:30) — owner: infra-ops.
- ben: PR for feature-flagged final-emit + metric, include tests — due EOD.
- ingrid: add an alert if truncated-stream-rate > 0.5% for 5m in region — due tomorrow.
- maya: will enable local retry/resume client flow and report back if any duplicates.

ingrid: Also adding a doc blurb for customers: \"If you operate behind aggressive NATs or client-side proxies, ensure upstream keepalive >= 30s or implement client-side reconnect logic that can dedupe partial streams.\"

deploy-bot: rollback: edge-proxy-config v2.13 restored to eu-west-1 at 2026-11-02T15:28:50 by infra-ops.

elle: Closing loop — @maya did you want us to keep the ticket open until PR and alert are in?

maya: Please keep open until PR lands; for now regression looks fixed on our end. Thanks everyone :heart:
